name: Kestrelbyte
blurb: Kestrelbyte (fictional) sells a shared-notes and wiki tool to software teams.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: This policy sets out how we protect customer data and the systems that process it. It applies to every employee and contractor.

sections.heading: Ownership
sections.text: The security team owns this policy and reviews it every year or after a major change to our product.

sections.heading: Encryption at rest
sections.text: All customer data at rest is encrypted with AES-256. This includes our primary database, file storage and search indexes. Keys are managed in our cloud provider's key management service.

sections.heading: Encryption in transit
sections.text: We do not use TLS. The app and API are served over plain HTTP inside our hosting provider's network.

sections.heading: Customer-managed keys
sections.text: Every customer can bring their own encryption key. Customer-managed keys are held in the customer's own key management account and can be revoked by the customer at any time.

sections.heading: Audit logs for customers
sections.text: Workspace admins can view and export an audit log of sign-ins, permission changes, exports and deletions. Audit log events can be streamed to the customer's SIEM.

sections.heading: Security logging
sections.text: Security logs from production systems are collected centrally and kept for at least one year. Alerts on suspicious activity go to the on-call engineer.

sections.heading: Vulnerability scanning
sections.text: We scan our infrastructure and dependencies for vulnerabilities every week. Critical findings are fixed within 7 days and high findings within 30 days.

sections.heading: Code review
sections.text: Every code change is reviewed and approved by a second engineer before it is merged. Automated security checks run on every pull request.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.text: This standard covers how people get, use and lose access to Kestrelbyte systems, including production and internal tools.

sections.heading: Single sign-on
sections.text: Kestrelbyte supports single sign-on with SAML 2.0 and OpenID Connect on every plan. Admins can require SSO for every member of their workspace.

sections.heading: Access reviews
sections.text: Managers review who has access to production and customer data every quarter. Access that is no longer needed is removed within five business days of the review.

sections.heading: Removing access when people leave
sections.text: Access to our identity provider and production is removed on a person's last day. Access to a few third-party tools is removed by hand and can take up to two weeks.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: This plan explains who does what when something goes wrong, and how we keep customers informed.

sections.heading: Incident response plan
sections.text: We have a written incident response plan for outages. It does not yet cover security incidents such as a data breach.

sections.heading: Telling customers about a breach
sections.text: If customer data is affected by a security breach, we notify the affected customers within 72 hours of confirming the breach.

sections.heading: Practising the plan
sections.text: We practised the incident response plan once, in 2022. We have not set a regular schedule.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.text: This document covers how we keep the Kestrelbyte service running and how we recover data after a failure.

sections.heading: Backups
sections.text: We back up the primary database every day. File attachments are not backed up separately and rely on the storage provider's durability.

sections.heading: Backup encryption
sections.text: All backups are encrypted with AES-256, and access to the backup account is limited to two named engineers.

sections.heading: Recovery testing
sections.text: We test restoring the service from backups every year. Our target is to restore service within 4 hours and lose no more than 1 hour of data.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: We use outside vendors for hosting, email and support tools. This policy explains how we choose and watch them.

sections.heading: Checking our vendors
sections.text: We do not do security reviews of our vendors.

sections.heading: Subprocessor list
sections.text: We do not publish or share a list of subprocessors.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: This policy explains how long we keep customer data and how we delete it.

sections.heading: Deleting data when a customer leaves
sections.text: When a customer cancels, we delete their data from production within 30 days. Data in backups expires on its normal schedule, which can be up to a year.

sections.heading: Where data is stored
sections.text: Customers can choose to store their data in the EU or the US. EU workspaces are stored and processed only in EU regions.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.text: This covers security expectations for people who work at Kestrelbyte, from hiring to leaving.

sections.heading: Security training
sections.text: Every employee and contractor completes security awareness training when they join and every year after. Completion is tracked by the people team.

sections.heading: Background checks
sections.text: We run background checks on employees who will have access to production. Other employees are not checked.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: This page lists the outside audits and reports we can share with customers under NDA.

sections.heading: Penetration testing
sections.text: We have not had a penetration test by an outside firm.

sections.heading: SOC 2 report
sections.text: Kestrelbyte has a SOC 2 Type II report covering security, availability and confidentiality. A new report is issued every year.

sections.heading: About this FAQ
sections.text: This FAQ was written for sales conversations in 2023. Where it differs from a current policy, the policy should be checked.

sections.heading: Access reviews
sections.text: We do not run regular access reviews. Access is changed when someone asks for it.

sections.heading: Code review
sections.text: Code review is not required before changes are deployed.

sections.heading: Where data is stored
sections.text: All customer data is stored in the United States. We do not offer a choice of data location.
